treaty_name: Agreement between Australia and Ireland for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with respect to Taxes on Income and Capital Gains (1983)
eif_quote: [1] Notes to this effect were exchanged 21 December 1983, on which date the Agreement entered into force. | Art. 29: "(a) in Australia- (i) with respect to withholding tax on income that is derived by a non-resident, in relation to income derived on or after 1 July in the calendar year immediately following that in which the Agreement enters into force; ... (b) in Ireland- (i) with respect to income tax and capital gains tax, for any year of assessment beginning on or after 6 April in the calendar year immediately following that in which the Agreement enters into force; (ii) with respect to corporation tax, for any financial year beginning on or after 1 January in the calendar year immediately following"
source_title: Australia-Ireland DTA [1983] ATS 25 (AustLII); ATO MLI synthesised text
source_url: https://www.austlii.edu.au/au/other/dfat/treaties/1983/25.html (read via web.archive.org/web/20260103201306) ; https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?DocID=MLI/MLI-Ireland-agreement (ATO synthesised text, read via web.archive.org/web/20240221044141)

rates.quote: Dividends paid by a company which is a resident of Australia for the purposes of Australian tax, being dividends to which a resident of Ireland is beneficially entitled, may be taxed in Ireland. Such dividends may also be taxed in Australia, according to the law of Australia, but the tax so charged shall not exceed 15 per cent of the gross amount of the dividends.

Except as aforesaid, dividends paid by a company which is a resident of Ireland for the purposes of Irish tax, being dividends to which a resident of Australia is beneficially entitled, shall be exempt from any tax in Ireland which is chargeable on dividends.

Such interest may be taxed in the Contracting State in which it arises, and according to the law of that State, but the tax so charged shall not exceed 10 per cent of the gross amount of the interest.

Such interest may be taxed in the Contracting State in which it arises, and according to the law of that State, but the tax so charged shall not exceed 10 per cent of the gross amount of the interest.

Such royalties may be taxed in the Contracting State in which they arise, and according to the law of that State, but the tax so charged shall not exceed 10 per cent of the gross amount of the royalties.

Such royalties may be taxed in the Contracting State in which they arise, and according to the law of that State, but the tax so charged shall not exceed 10 per cent of the gross amount of the royalties.

ppt.quote: Notwithstanding any provisions of [the Agreement], a benefit under [the Agreement] shall not be granted in respect of an item of income [...] if it is reasonable to conclude, having regard to all relevant facts and circumstances, that obtaining that benefit was one of the principal purposes of any arrangement or transaction that resulted directly or indirectly in that benefit, unless it is established that granting that benefit in these circumstances would be in accordance with the object and purpose of the relevant provisions of [the Agreement].

notes: Article numbering: Dividends = Art. 11, Interest = Art. 12, Royalties = Art. 13. Dividends asymmetric: Australia-source capped at 15%; Ireland-source dividends exempt from Irish tax chargeable on dividends (Art. 11(2)(c)), except that under Art. 11(2)(b) Ireland may tax at up to 15% the dividend plus Irish tax credit where an Australian resident is entitled to the Irish tax credit under Art. 11(3) (the Irish imputation tax credit no longer exists, so this exception is understood to be obsolete). Art. 11(6) anti-abuse rule for >=10% holdings acquired to access old profits. Treaty anti-abuse sentences in Arts 11(6), 12(7) and 13 replaced (in part) by MLI arts 7(1)/7(4) per ATO synthesised text; MLI WHT effect from 2020-01-01. Treaty does not separately define the Irish WHT start date: Irish valid_from uses the income tax year of assessment start (6 April 1984); Australian WHT from 1 July 1984.
unverified: Irish valid_from 1984-04-06 (treaty gives income tax year of assessment / corporation tax financial year, not a WHT-specific date)
Treatment of Ireland-source dividends as exclusive relies on the obsolescence of the Irish tax credit referred to in Art. 11(2)(b)/(3)
